title: ACME DNS-01 through acme-dns, so any DNS provider works after one CNAME
description:
Split out of bead mimid-e13m.8, which built the ACME core and
`dns = "hook"`. docs/design/frontend-auth.md §5.2 rank 2 names acme-dns as
the third way to write the DNS-01 TXT record, and the one that "turns any
provider into one that works, after one CNAME by hand".

HOW IT WORKS. acme-dns is a small DNS server made for exactly this. The
user registers once, gets a subdomain and credentials, and puts a CNAME
from `_acme-challenge.chat.example.org` at it. From then on the agent
POSTs the challenge value to the acme-dns instance's `/update` with its
credentials, and acme-dns serves the TXT record. The agent never touches
the real zone, and the credentials can only write that one subdomain,
which is why §5.2 ranks it as it does.

WHAT IT NEEDS. An HTTP POST with two headers (`X-Api-User`,
`X-Api-Key`) and a JSON body of the subdomain and the value. That is
small: the agent already has an HTTP client, and the `acme` module already
has the seam (`write_record`, which the hook method goes through).
Estimate 100 lines with tests, which is why this is worth doing and bead
mimid-e13m.8.1 (RFC 2136) may not be.

CONFIGURATION, extending §5.3:

    [tls.acme]
    dns = "acme-dns"
    acme-dns = { url = "https://auth.acme-dns.io", username = "...",
                 password = "...", subdomain = "..." }

The password is a secret: redacted in Debug, never logged, and the table
is better read from a file the registration wrote than pasted into the
configuration -- decide which when writing it.

TESTS, OFFLINE. A fake acme-dns over the same hand-rolled HTTPS server
tests/acme.rs already has for the fake ACME authority, asserting the two
headers and the body, and that a refusal fails the order rather than
letting it go on to a challenge the authority will fail.

DEPENDS ON mimid-e13m.8's core, which is built.
